neighbours.label: the 'of' (or 'price') in bargain cost-comparison phrases: something bought or done 'for a fraction of', 'for the price of', 'for the sum of' an amount; the same nouns used for plain quantities ('a fraction of the students', 'the price of bread rose') stay low
fire: The outlet sells last year's jackets at a fraction of the original cost.
For the price of one dinner out, you can cook for a whole week.
The old mill was sold in 1880 for the sum of nine hundred pounds.
Generic tablets work just as well for a fraction of the brand price.
We rented a whole cabin for the price of a single hotel room.
Cloud servers now do the job for a fraction of what the hardware cost.
The estate was bought by the town for the modest sum of ten dollars.
Students can get the software for a fraction of the retail price.
quiet: The survey found that a fraction of the jackets had faulty zips.
The price of one dinner out has doubled in the last five years.
The old mill was the largest building in the town in 1880.
Only a fraction of the patients reported any side effects.
The sum of the two numbers is always an even number.
The price of a hotel room rises sharply in the summer.
Cloud servers now handle a large share of the company's traffic.
Students can get help with the software from the library staff.

predictions: bargain cost phrases 0.5-1.0; plain fraction/sum/price uses below 0.2
short: 'of' in 'for a fraction/the price of' cost phrases
notes: Card peaks on ' of' after 'a fraction', 'the price', 'the sum' in purchase contexts. Probe: at a fraction of the supermarket price 1.008, for the price of some bikes 0.953, sold the farm for the sum of 0.653, for the price I was paying 0.498; a fraction of the students 0.078, sum of the angles 0.095, price of bread rose 0.108.
